title: Evidence 103-141 Safety Reconciliation and FP-027 Open Status
claim: FP-MCP-268 records a coherent reconciliation of evidence IDs 103 through 141, explicitly confirming that FP-MCP-217 was revised by FP-MCP-236, the FP-MCP-233 approval reuse window was closed by live expiry/stale-clearance evidence, FP-MCP-265 was an HTTP single-shot canary rather than a guarded runner start, and original FP-027 guarded-start discipline remains unsatisfied end-to-end.
summary: Record the reviewer-accepted accounting for the omitted evidence range 103 through 141 before any further lifecycle work. This checkpoint names FP-MCP-235 as the reconciliation opener, FP-MCP-236 as the deliberate popup-mediated clearance policy revision, FP-MCP-237 as the historical integrity review of FP-MCP-233, FP-MCP-238 as the live approval-death/fix-activation verification, FP-MCP-239 through FP-MCP-265 as the HTTP tooling and lifecycle chain, and FP-MCP-266/267 as operator workflow trace instrumentation and legacy normalization. It also records two open safety items: the popup-mediated clearance posture needs explicit human-attention/UX display requirements, and the original FP-027 guarded-runner-start discipline has still never been fully satisfied end-to-end with process-tree snapshot and live abort-readiness at the moment of runner start contact.
caveats: This checkpoint is an accounting/reconciliation record, not new implementation work.
This checkpoint does not revise FP-MCP-236; it records an additional follow-up requirement for popup approval human-attention/UX controls.
This checkpoint does not run FP-027 and does not contact the runner start endpoint.
This checkpoint does not declare FP-027 satisfied by FP-MCP-233 or by FP-MCP-265.
This checkpoint does not mutate or rewrite prior evidence files, including overwritten per-packet v1o result artifacts that remain recoverable through git history.
